answer: Each agent must post a bonded LP position in a shallow meadow pool, so every new identity pays real slippage to enter. A fake identity's stake emits a plume of on-chain footprint that the bonding curve prices against it, making depth expensive to fake. Cost per sybil scales with pool depth, but a sparrow-sized attacker can still split across pools, so bonding depth caps, not eliminates, the attack.
